mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deepening labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns remain positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 1% month-over-month, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and cost margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate higher earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% AND UNRATE change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both show positive monthly changes for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.7% for five consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which increases corporate revenues and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.7% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1.2%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
